Case 60516 (diabetic patient, no glucose obs) fired a-preop-glucose -> alert 'Check Glucose'; case 28249 (p-dilation-and-curettage, no doxycycline) fired a-preop-doxycycline-check -> 'Doxycycline PO Not Given Preoperatively'. The 8 residual Uncategorized rules are i-fluid-infusion-medication, i-last-local-anesthetic, i-latest-glucose, i-latest-medication, w-antibiotic-previous-doses, w-calcium-blood-transfusion, w-fluconazole-slow-administer, w-weight-type-adjustment. w-dantrolene-default-dose reads 'Wrong Dose', which is what the commit message said PR #4341 already handled.
evidence.red_check: Two flips, both reverted. (1) I checked out the parent commit (2b76db076^) versions of all 36 changed rule classes, compiled them inside the app container with javac against /app/jib-classpath-file plus a lombok jar (41 class files, inner-class sets matched the shipped ones exactly), backed up the shipped classes with md5sums, swapped the pre-fix classes into /app/classes and restarted. The map went red: Diabetes Management disappeared entirely, Monitoring rose from 2 to 15, Uncategorized from 8 to 31, and the same real firings re-attributed to 'Monitoring | a-preop-glucose' and 'Uncategorized | a-preop-doxycycline-check'. I restored the 41 backed-up classes and confirmed all 41 md5sums match the shipped set, then confirmed the regenerated rule_definitions dump is identical to the original post-fix dump. (2) For a log-visible red, I compiled the parent commit's GuidanceCategory enum (no DIABETES_MANAGEMENT constant) and dropped it into /app/classes so it shadowed the orci-models jar, with the shipped rule classes in place. Startup failed with 'Caused by: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: No enum constant com.guided.orci.engine.rule.GuidanceCategory.DIABETES_MANAGEMENT' while Spring read PostInsulinGlucoseCheckAppLaunchRule's annotation — proof the running image really carries the new constant. I removed the shadow class, restarted, verified the rule classes still match shipped md5sums and the category map is back to the post-fix dump, and fired a-preop-glucose on a brand-new case (92243) which attributed to 'Diabetes Management' again.

automation.assessment: There is no test anywhere that pins a rule's guidance category. The four Java tests that mention GuidanceCategory only stub it (RuleExecutionResultServiceTest returns UNCATEGORIZED from a fake annotation); the qa-suite has no reference to guidance categories at all. That matters because the category is annotation metadata with a silent default: a new rule that omits guidanceCategory ships as UNCATEGORIZED and quietly lands in the analytics 'Uncategorized' bucket, which is exactly the drift this ticket was cleaning up. RuleIdentifierConventionTest already establishes the right pattern for this kind of guard (classpath-scan every @RuleDefinition and assert an invariant), so the new tests belong beside it rather than in the qa-suite.
proposed_tests: orci: classpath-scan every @RuleDefinition and assert no rule is UNCATEGORIZED except an explicit allowlist of the 8 known info/warning rules, so any new rule forces a category decision at build time.

orci: assert every rule whose identifier or class is insulin/glucose/hypoglycemia-related declares GuidanceCategory.DIABETES_MANAGEMENT, locking the 13-rule bucket this ticket created against a silent slide back to MONITORING.
orci: assert MONITORING is now claimed only by the coagulation-lab rules (a-preop-pt-inr, a-preop-ptt), the negative half of the same move.

jira_comment:
Validated against a throwaway build of main (e7eeafd6c) with a live app and DB. Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: I staged two demo cases and fired real rules through the app. a-preop-glucose fired for a diabetic patient with no glucose result, and a-preop-doxycycline-check fired on a D&C case. Joining those firings to rule_definitions the way the analytics reports do, they land in Diabetes Management and Delayed/Missed/Wrong Antibiotic. The full new map is live in every tenant schema, with Diabetes Management holding 13 rules.

Negative: nothing moved that should not have. I compared the full 114-rule category map before and after the change and exactly 36 rules differ, matching the 36 changed files one for one. No insulin or glucose rule is left in Monitoring; Monitoring is now just the two coag-lab rules, a-preop-pt-inr and a-preop-ptt.

Red check: I compiled the pre-change versions of all 36 rule classes, swapped them into the running container and restarted. Diabetes Management vanished, Monitoring went from 2 to 15, Uncategorized from 8 to 31, and the same firings re-attributed to Monitoring and Uncategorized. I also swapped in the old enum on its own and startup failed on the missing DIABETES_MANAGEMENT constant. Both flips were reverted and I confirmed the restore by checksum and by re-firing the rule.

One thing I could not check: the CSV attached to this ticket is not readable from my environment, so I verified the delivered mapping is real and complete, not that it equals the CSV. These are still uncategorized if any of them were meant to move: i-fluid-infusion-medication, i-last-local-anesthetic, i-latest-glucose, i-latest-medication, w-antibiotic-previous-doses, w-calcium-blood-transfusion, w-fluconazole-slow-administer, w-weight-type-adjustment.

Automation: nothing pins guidance categories today, and the annotation silently defaults to Uncategorized. I plan a classpath-scan test next to RuleIdentifierConventionTest that fails when a new rule ships uncategorized, plus tests locking the diabetes bucket and the reduced Monitoring bucket.
